about: Dashboard lines: one is shown in the hero on every dashboard load. Public file: facts, history, rules of thumb and quotes only, never internal information. Rules and the refresh routine: docs/LINES.md. Check with: node dev/lines-check.mjs

lines.text: In 1902 Willis Carrier designed a system to control humidity at a Brooklyn printing plant. It is widely counted as the start of modern air conditioning.
Carrier's patent "Apparatus for Treating Air" was granted on 2 January 1906.
The term "air conditioning" was coined in 1906 by Stuart Cramer, a textile engineer in North Carolina.
In 1911 Carrier presented his "Rational Psychrometric Formulae" to ASME. The psychrometric chart still rests on that work.
John Gorrie, a Florida physician, was granted a US patent for an ice-making machine in 1851. He built it to cool his patients' rooms.
Jacob Perkins patented a vapour-compression refrigeration machine in Britain in 1834: the cycle almost every chiller still uses.
In 1824 Sadi Carnot published the theory that sets the efficiency limit of every heat engine and every refrigeration machine.
Lord Kelvin described the heat pump in 1852: a machine that moves heat from a cold place to a warmer one.
Carrier introduced the centrifugal chiller in 1922, which opened the way to cooling large buildings.
In 1925 the Rivoli Theatre in New York opened with Carrier cooling, and summer cinema-going took off.
The US House of Representatives was air conditioned in 1928 and the Senate in 1929.
CFC-12, sold as Freon, was developed around 1930 by Thomas Midgley Jr. and colleagues as a non-toxic, non-flammable refrigerant.
In 1974 Mario Molina and Sherwood Rowland showed that CFCs could destroy stratospheric ozone. They shared the 1995 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Paul Crutzen.
The Montreal Protocol (1987) was the first UN treaty ratified by every member state. It phased out CFCs and is phasing out HCFCs.
The Kigali Amendment (2016) brought HFCs under the Montreal Protocol. It entered into force on 1 January 2019.
ASHRAE was formed in 1959 by merging ASHAE (founded 1894) and ASRE (founded 1904).
AHRI was formed on 1 January 2008 by merging ARI and GAMA.
Eurovent was founded in 1958. Its Eurovent Certified Performance mark checks that published equipment ratings hold up in test.
Daikin was founded in Osaka in 1924 as Osaka Kinzoku Kogyosho by Akira Yamada.
"Daikin" is short for Osaka Kinzoku (Osaka Metal): "Dai" from the first character of Osaka, "Kin" from kinzoku.
Daikin developed Japan's first packaged air conditioner in 1951.
In 1982 Daikin introduced VRV: one outdoor unit varying refrigerant flow to many indoor units.
In 2012 Daikin launched the world's first air conditioner using R-32.
In 2015 Daikin gave free worldwide access to its basic patents for air conditioners using R-32.
Persian yakhchāls, domed ice houses fed by qanat water, stored winter ice through desert summers for centuries.
The Gulf's barjeel (wind tower) catches the breeze above the roofline and turns it down into the rooms. Dubai's Al Fahidi district still has many.
Roman baths and villas were heated by the hypocaust: furnace gases ran under raised floors and up through flues in the walls.
In 1758 Benjamin Franklin and John Hadley evaporated ether on a thermometer bulb and drove it well below freezing on a warm day.
Ferdinand Carré built an ammonia-water absorption refrigeration machine around 1859, the ancestor of today's absorption chillers.
Carl von Linde built a practical ammonia compression refrigeration machine in the 1870s. Breweries were among the first users.
Legionnaires' disease is named after a 1976 outbreak at an American Legion convention in Philadelphia, traced to the hotel's cooling system.
The Burj Khalifa collects about 15 million gallons of condensate a year from its cooling equipment and uses it to water the park at its base.
Benjamin Franklin's "an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure" (1735) was advice on fire safety in Philadelphia.
Franklin designed his stove around 1742 to heat a room with less wood than an open fireplace.
Packard offered the first factory car air conditioning, on its 1940 models.
The Celsius scale first ran backwards: in 1742 Anders Celsius set 0 for boiling water and 100 for freezing.
EN 779 filter classes (G4, F7 …) were withdrawn in 2018. ISO 16890 rates filters by ePM1, ePM2.5 and ePM10 instead.
On 23 December 1919 Alice H. Parker of New Jersey was granted US patent 1,325,905 for a gas-fired furnace sending warm air through ducts to separate rooms, each unit switched on its own.
Warren S. Johnson patented his electric room thermostat in 1883 and founded the Johnson Electric Service Company in Milwaukee in 1885.
In 1856 Peter von Rittinger in Austria applied the heat pump principle, reusing the latent heat of water vapour to evaporate salt brine.
The Equitable Building in Portland, Oregon (1948) was the first large US commercial building heated and cooled by heat pumps, drawing on two wells.
On 16 May 1985 Joe Farman, Brian Gardiner and Jonathan Shanklin of the British Antarctic Survey reported the Antarctic ozone hole in Nature.
The Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer was adopted on 22 March 1985, two years before the Montreal Protocol that put it into action.
In 1850 James Joule published his paddle-wheel measurements: about 772 ft·lbf of work raises 1 lb of water by 1 °F, the mechanical equivalent of heat.
Schuyler Skaats Wheeler built one of the first electric fans in 1882, a two-blade desk fan driven by an electric motor.
One ton of refrigeration is the heat to melt one short ton of ice in 24 hours: 12,000 BTU/h, about 3.517 kW.
1 kW = 3,412 BTU/h, so COP = EER ÷ 3.412.
Fan laws: flow follows speed, pressure follows speed squared, power follows speed cubed. Slow a fan by 20% and its power drops by about half.
Sensible heat of air: Q (W) is about 1.2 × airflow (L/s) × ΔT (K).
Imperial shortcuts: Q (BTU/h) = 1.08 × cfm × ΔT (°F) for air, and 500 × gpm × ΔT (°F) for water.
At a 10 °F (5.6 K) rise, one ton of cooling needs about 2.4 gpm of chilled water.
1 m³/s is about 2,119 cfm, and 1 inch of water gauge is about 249 Pa.
IPLV (AHRI 550/590) weights chiller efficiency at 100/75/50/25% load by 1/42/45/12%. Part load is where a chiller spends its life.
Carnot's limit for cooling: COP = T_cold ÷ (T_hot − T_cold), in kelvin. Every degree of lift costs efficiency.
Air at sea level weighs about 1.2 kg per cubic metre: a 10 × 10 × 3 m room holds about 360 kg of air.
Evaporating 1 kg of water takes about 2,450 kJ. That is the energy behind latent load and evaporative cooling.
lines.source: latent heat of water at about 20 C

lines.text: A seated person gives off roughly 100–120 W of heat, part sensible and part latent.
lines.source: ASHRAE Fundamentals, heat gain from occupants

lines.text: Outdoor CO₂ is now around 420 ppm. Indoor levels well above 1,000 ppm usually mean too little outdoor air.
lines.source: NOAA global CO2; common ventilation indicator
IPCC AR4, as used in EU F-gas Regulation

lines.text: R-717 (ammonia) has zero ozone depletion and zero GWP, and has run industrial refrigeration since the 1870s.
Any surface colder than the air's dew point collects condensate. That is why chilled-water pipes need vapour-sealed insulation.
A cooling tower can bring water close to the air's wet-bulb temperature but never below it. The gap is called the approach.
Double a round duct's diameter and, at the same airflow, its friction loss falls to about one-thirtieth.
Relative humidity changes whenever air temperature changes. Humidity ratio (g/kg) only changes when moisture is added or removed.
Two equal noise sources together are 3 dB louder than one, and a 10 dB rise sounds roughly twice as loud.
Per cubic metre, water holds about 3,500 times as much heat as air. That is why a small pipe can do the work of a large duct.
MERV ratings come from ASHRAE 52.2; ePM ratings come from ISO 16890. They are not one-to-one.
AMCA 210 (also ASHRAE 51) is the laboratory method for rating fan airflow and pressure.
NFPA 90A sets the fire-safety rules for air-conditioning and ventilating systems, including where fire and smoke dampers go.
Chilled or hot water: Q (kW) = 4.19 × flow (L/s) × ΔT (K). At a 5 K difference, 1 L/s carries about 21 kW.
lines.source: arithmetic: c_p water 4.19 kJ/(kg·K), 1 L = 1 kg; 4.19 × 1 × 5 = 20.95 kW

lines.text: Fan shaft power (W) = airflow (m³/s) × total pressure (Pa) ÷ efficiency. 2 m³/s at 500 Pa and 65% needs about 1.5 kW.
Quick dew point: subtract (100 − RH) ÷ 5 from the air temperature in °C. Good to about 1 K when RH is above 50%.
lines.source: Lawrence, M. G., Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society 86(2), 2005

lines.text: Air changes per hour = airflow (m³/h) ÷ room volume (m³). 300 m³/h into a 100 m³ room is 3 ACH.
In open air, doubling the distance from a point noise source lowers the sound level by about 6 dB.
Three-phase power: P = √3 × V × I × PF. At 400 V, 10 A and a power factor of 0.9 that is about 6.2 kW.
10 m of water column is about 98 kPa, close to 1 bar, and 1 bar is about 14.5 psi.
lines.source: arithmetic: 1,000 kg/m³ × 9.81 m/s² × 10 m = 98.1 kPa; 1 bar = 14.504 psi

lines.text: Heat through a wall or window: Q = U × A × ΔT. 10 m² at U = 0.5 W/(m²·K) with a 20 K difference passes 100 W.
One may see the possibility of freezing a man to death on a warm summer's day.
When you can measure what you are speaking about, and express it in numbers, you know something about it.
If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of Giants.
Chance favours only the prepared mind.
The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.
The first principle is that you must not fool yourself, and you are the easiest person to fool.
Perfection is achieved not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing left to take away.
lines.source: Terre des hommes (Wind, Sand and Stars), 1939

lines.text: He who has begun is half done. Dare to be wise.
A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
Give me a place to stand, and I will move the Earth.
lines.source: as reported by Pappus of Alexandria

lines.text: Simplicity is prerequisite for reliability.
Nature, to be commanded, must be obeyed.
Genius is one per cent inspiration and ninety-nine per cent perspiration.
Measure twice, cut once.
Nothing is too wonderful to be true, if it be consistent with the laws of nature.
lines.source: laboratory journal entry 10,040, 19 March 1849; Bence Jones, The Life and Letters of Faraday, vol. II, 1870

lines.text: It is not because things are difficult that we do not dare; it is because we do not dare that they are difficult.
lines.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 104.26 (Gummere translation)

lines.text: Knowing is not enough; we must apply. Willing is not enough; we must do.
lines.source: Wilhelm Meisters Wanderjahre, 1829 (Betrachtungen im Sinne der Wanderer)

lines.text: Melting 1 kg of ice absorbs about 334 kJ, as much heat as warming that water from 0 °C to about 80 °C.
lines.source: arithmetic: latent heat of fusion 334 kJ/kg ÷ 4.19 kJ/(kg·K) = 79.7 K

lines.text: The IEA's Future of Cooling (2018) counted about 1.6 billion air conditioners in use and projected 5.6 billion by 2050.
CO₂ (R-744) has its critical point at about 31 °C and 74 bar. Above that it cannot condense, so in hot weather CO₂ systems run transcritical.
Water boils at 5 °C at about 0.87 kPa, roughly 1/116 of sea-level pressure. That is why absorption chillers run under deep vacuum.
lines.source: IAPWS steam tables: saturation pressure at 5 °C 0.8726 kPa; 101.325 / 0.8726 = 116

lines.text: Refrigerant numbers encode the molecule: R-134a is C₂H₂F₄. First digit carbons − 1, second hydrogens + 1, third fluorines.
Since 20 May 2019 the kelvin is defined by fixing the Boltzmann constant at exactly 1.380649 × 10⁻²³ J/K.
lines.source: BIPM, The International System of Units (SI brochure), 9th edition, 2019

lines.text: Montreal Protocol parties met in Kigali on 2–6 November 2026 (MOP38), ten years after the Kigali Amendment on HFCs was agreed there, and agreed new Multilateral Fund money.
Daikin Applied expanded its Modular Solutions plant in Phoenix, Arizona, from 58,000 to 191,000 ft² (about 17,700 m²) in October 2026.
From 1 January 2027 the EU F-gas Regulation 2024/573 bans new self-contained air conditioners and heat pumps up to 12 kW using refrigerant of GWP 150 or more.
